correctness.rationale: The anchored rooted-tree difference operator D is invertible, and its inverse columns are indicators of rooted descendant subtrees. Exterior derivative of Euclidean projection equals R/||x||_2 (I-uu^T), whose induced D-l1 norm reduces via sign duality and the smaller rank-two eigenvalue to (s_v+sqrt(|T_v|)||D^T s||_2)/2. The alternating-depth sign vector simultaneously saturates each |s_v-sum_child s_w|<=1+d_v; the root column |T_r|=n yields exactly (1+sqrt(n sum(1+d_v)^2))/2. Integrating derivatives across any segment proves the global bound and strict nonattainment, and tangent boundary pairs approach it. The child-degree square identity S=3n-2+sum d_v^2 gives endpoint-rooted-path minimum 4n-3 and center-star maximum n^2+n-1. Independent signs/subtree checks on rooted path, star and branched examples reproduce the exact constants; finite diagnostics do not prove every rooted tree.
